Latvian Gas & Water Utilities Workers Walk Out, Disrupting Services Across Country

RIGA—Gas and water supply across Latvia faced significant disruption on Thursday as thousands of workers in the utilities sector began a coordinated walkout, demanding higher wages and improved working conditions. The strike, affecting key suppliers such as Baltu Enerģija and Rīgas Ūdens Tīkls, entered its second day with no immediate resolution in sight.

According to the Latvian Utilities Workers Union (LUWU), more than 3,000 employees have participated in the industrial action, resulting in reduced pressure and intermittent service in several regions, particularly in Riga and Liepāja. Customers reported delayed gas deliveries and water supply interruptions in some residential and commercial neighborhoods.

“The current wage levels do not reflect the rising costs our members face,” said LUWU chair Ilze Kalniņa in a press conference. “We are willing to negotiate, but so far, management has not met us halfway.”

Industry observers highlight the strike’s impact on operational stability. Data from the Latvian Gas and Water Association indicate that daily gas distribution volumes dropped by an estimated 28% on Wednesday, while water supply output fell by as much as 19% in affected municipalities.

Baltu Enerģija spokesperson Jānis Ozols said, “We respect our employees’ right to take action, but the ongoing disruption threatens to undermine public trust in essential services. We urge the union to return to the bargaining table.”

Negotiations between union representatives and company managements have reportedly stalled over the size and timeline of proposed wage increases. The Ministry of Economic Affairs called for a swift resolution, warning that prolonged disruptions could have “serious consequences for households and infrastructure.”

As of Thursday afternoon, both sides remained at an impasse, with union officials vowing to continue the walkout until their demands are addressed. No timeline for resumption of normal services has been announced.
